statements.text: For two algebraic fractions with a common denominator, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f2(x): the sum is (f1(x)+f3(x))/f2(x). Formula: $n_1(x)+n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)+f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}$

With a common denominator, the difference is (f1(x) - f3(x))/f2(x), also written as f1(x)/f2(x) + (-f3(x))/f2(x). Formula: $n_1(x)-n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}-\frac{f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{-f_3(x)}{f_2(x)}$

For two algebraic fractions with different denominators, n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x), n2(x)=f3(x)/f4(x): the sum is (f1(x)×f4(x)+f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)). Formula: $n_1(x)+n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}+\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)\times f_4(x)+f_3(x)\times f_2(x)}{f_2(x)\times f_4(x)}$

With different denominators, the difference is (f1(x)×f4(x) - f3(x)×f2(x))/(f2(x)×f4(x)). Formula: $n_1(x)-n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}-\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)\times f_4(x)-f_3(x)\times f_2(x)}{f_2(x)\times f_4(x)}$

context.text: Imagine one tap can fill a water tank alone in $x$ hours, and a second tap can fill the same tank alone in $(x+2)$ hours. In one hour the first tap fills $\frac{1}{x}$ of the tank and the second fills $\frac{1}{x+2}$ of it. Write the part of the tank filled in one hour by both taps together as a single fraction, and say which values of $x$ are not allowed.

statements.text: If n1(x)=f1(x)/f2(x) and n2(x)=f3(x)/f4(x) are two algebraic fractions, then their product is the product of numerators over the product of denominators, where x is in the common domain of the two fractions, i.e. R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f4)). Formula: $n_1(x)\times n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}\times\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)\times f_3(x)}{f_2(x)\times f_4(x)}$, domain $\mathbb{R}-(Z(f_2)\cup Z(f_4))$

Dividing two algebraic fractions means multiplying the first by the reciprocal of the second; the domain of n1 ÷ n2 is the common domain of n1, n2, n2^-1, i.e. R − (Z(f2) ∪ Z(f3) ∪ Z(f4)). Formula: $n_1(x)\div n_2(x)=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}\div\frac{f_3(x)}{f_4(x)}=\frac{f_1(x)}{f_2(x)}\times\frac{f_4(x)}{f_3(x)}$, domain $\mathbb{R}-(Z(f_2)\cup Z(f_3)\cup Z(f_4))$

context.text: Suppose a phone plan charges $\frac{x+3}{x-1}$ pounds for each unit of data, and you use $\frac{x-1}{x+5}$ units. The total cost is the product of the two fractions. Work out the total cost as a fraction in simplest form, and say which values of $x$ are not allowed.
